title: Retry refunds the way the platform allows

blocks.text: The payment service sends charges and refunds to the bank. A charge sent twice charges the customer twice, so a `Payment` is tried once. A refund carries the key of the charge it reverses, and the bank applies it once however often it arrives, so refunds implement the platform team's `Idempotent` interface, which says how often an idempotent operation may be tried. The platform team sets that number from its configuration and changes it when the bank's limits change.

items: `send(...)`: try a payment until the bank accepts it or the payment has used its attempts;
`Refund.maxAttempts()`: how many times a refund may be tried.

blocks.text: When you're done, charges are still sent once, and a failing refund is tried exactly as often as the platform's policy allows at the time, today and after the platform changes it. About five lines in total.

cases.says: a charge is sent exactly once, and send reports whether the bank accepted it
sending stops at the first attempt the bank accepts
a refund is tried as many times as the idempotency policy allows, not once like other payments
a refund's attempts follow the platform's policy when the platform raises or lowers it

origin.section: A Class Method Beats a Default, a More Specific Interface Beats Its Parent, and Any Other Conflict Is Yours to Resolve

concepts: A method declared in a class or inherited from a superclass wins over an interface default, even when called through the interface; the default is reached with X.super.m().
